lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the four-repo sm75 sibling ecosystem is real, 2026-active, and internally stratified: one full serving fork (weekly releases), one single-kernel adaptation fork (one-shot, May 2026), one high-velocity engine (daily commits, multi-contributor), one pedagogical kernel repo (single-day dump). (1) weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive: 815 stars, 123 forks, 160 commits, 12 open issues/10 PRs; two release lines - v0.1.x on upstream vLLM 0.21.0 (CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128, runtime identity vllm-sm75-tp2-cu128) ending at v0.1.17 (2026-08-24, 'last snapshot for 0.1.x'), and v0.2.x pre-releases v0.2.1-pre (2026-08-16) / pre2 (2026-08-21) / pre3 (2026-08-27) on upstream vLLM v0.27.1 with CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13, Python 3.12 'SM75 migration' - i.e. the house-ratified finding 'their v0.2.x = upstream v0.27.1 + one FlashInfer floor constant' (the fork privately restores the FlashInfer sm75 floor that upstream v0.24.0 raised to SM80). What it carries: Marlin kernels for FP8/INT4/NVFP4 weight routes, FlashInfer (attention, sampling, quantized paths), FlashQLA GDN/linear-attention prefill including the author's own FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 adaptation, TurboQuant K8V4 KV compression + INT8 KV, CUTLASS/Triton kernels; launcher/profile system (profiles/<model>/<mode>/<weight>/<route>.env, safe/normal/fast/aggressive). Model routes: Qwen3.x 27B primary (Qwen3.6 baseline claims 100+ tok/s single-request decode), Qwen3.x 35B MoE secondary, Gemma4 31B experimental; v0.2.1-pre3 adds validated Qwen3.8 27B FP8/NVFP4 profiles - directly tracking the operator's Qwen3.8 focus. MTP is built in with MTP3 presets per route and task-sensitivity docs (house-landed: MTP3 91 tok/s GPTQ-INT4 on dual 22GB; v0.2.1-pre2 4K/128 FP16-KV test reads '1522.72 / 75.83 with MTP3' vs '1570.57 / 30.01' without - as written, prefill slightly down and decode ~2.5x up [uncertain: metric order]). CUDA Graph validated non-eager TP=2/PP=1 (pre2), green for FP16 and TurboQuant-KV routes on Qwen 27B, partial for INT8 KV, fallback/admission issues on Gemma4 INT8/TurboQuant. TurboQuant engineering is visible in release hygiene: bounding the TurboQuant FlashInfer prefill wrapper cache CUDA-graph-safe (#132), reserving TurboQuant continuation workspace before KV-cache sizing (#134), TQK8V4 fixes (v0.1.12/13); MXFP4 explicitly unsupported on SM75 via upstream Marlin kernels. Maintenance health: ~weekly release cadence late Jun-Aug 2026, latest release 11 days before this survey; commits page rendered empty on fetch so last-commit date unverified [uncertain]. (2) weicj/FlashQLA-SM70-SM75: MIT fork of QwenLM/FlashQLA (TileLang-based GDN kernel library; upstream v0.1.0 released 2026-04-28, SM90+ CUDA 12.8+ PyTorch 2.8+, claims 2-3x forward / 2x backward over the FLA Triton kernel on Hopper). The fork adds exactly one thing: flash_qla.ops.gated_delta_rule.legacy.chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_legacy, a lazy-built forward-only CUDA extension for SM70/SM75-class Gated DeltaNet inference (landed 2026-05-18); explicitly NOT: backward/training, auto-dispatch from the high-level API, or SM80-class claims; SM75 (2080 Ti) validated, SM70 compile-check only. Measured: standalone kernel B=1,T=512,Hq=16,Hv=32,D=128 ~1.126 ms control vs ~0.520-0.533 ms legacy (~2.1x GDN-stage), GGUF runtime 406.656 -> 195.105 ms (~2.08x); whole-request prefill +7.17%, decode +0.61%, wall time -3.49% (house-landed finding: kernel 2.1x but decode e2e +0.61%). 10 stars, 6 forks, 21 commits; upstream/community burst Apr 28-May 7 (l2norm dtype fix, backward-grad-count fix, auto-cp UnboundLocal fix), owner's sm75 work a single day. Positioning: 'upstreamable experimental branch', a separate explicit legacy entry point. (3) ik_llama.cpp (ikawrakow): MIT llama.cpp fork since 2024-06, last upstream sync 2024-08 - an independent line, not a rebase rider; 3.2k stars, 456 forks, ~4876 commits; maintenance health strongest of the four: ~22-25 commits/week, multi-contributor (ikawrakow, joelfarthing, SamuelOliveirads, sayap, guy915), last commit 2026-09-03. CUDA backend explicitly supports 'Turing or newer'. What it carries that matters for crosspoll: MLA/FlashMLA (FlashMLA-3 on CPU; CUDA on Ampere+ per PR 386), IQK quant family (IQ2_K-IQ6_K, KS/R4 variants, IQ4_KSS/IQ2_KL, Trellis IQ1_KT-IQ4_KT, MXFP4 for gpt-oss, regex quant mixes), KV-cache quantization Q8_KV plus low-perplexity Q4_0 with Hadamard transforms for K- and V-cache (Q8_0 cache works with MLA), MTP decoding for GLM-4.x MoE / Qwen 3.5/3.6 / Gemma 4 / GLM 5 / Step 3.7 and - directly on the operator's focus - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: runtime support 'qwen4exp' #2365 (2026-08-27), 'MTP (NextN) self-speculative decoding support' #2369 (2026-09-02), standalone Qwen3.5 MTP GGUFs via -md #2328, plus scheduler discipline 'charge the generation budget per accepted token' #2358; other spec lanes: ngram #1261 / suffix #1646 self-spec, DFlash/DFlash-2/DSpark drafting; hybrid CPU/GPU inference (--cpu-moe, auto-fit offload, graph split); gemma4 compacted SWA KV --swa-compress #2378 and SWA compression with DFlash/DSpark #2384. The README's TL;DR is itself the crosspoll thesis: MLA, quant repacking, fused delta-net (upstream name GDN), tensor parallel, MTP, and DFlash all 'appeared here first before becoming available in llama.cpp'. TurboQuant inside ik_llama: community standalone implementation, issue #1509 (2026-03-25, closed): CPU complete 18/18 tests (quantize/dequantize/rotation/bit-packing in ggml_turboquant.c), CUDA kernels written incl. a fused attention dot product but awaiting GPU validation; round-trip MSE b=3 0.034144 (~paper's 0.034), b=4 0.009253; TQ3 52 vs 256 B/128-block = 4.9x, TQ4 68 B = 3.8x; no integration into ik_llama.cpp itself (6-phase spec submitted, unreviewed); maintainer counter-position in discussion #1528: his Hadamard-transform q4_0 KV 'wipes the floor with TurboQuant at about the same KV cache memory footprint'. IQ_K/IQ_KS merging into llama.cpp mainline was in progress March 2026 [uncertain: completion]. (4) johnscheuer/flash-attention-sm75: from-scratch CUDA FlashAttention v1 forward pass for SM75 via WMMA tensor cores (Turing lacks Ampere features; 40 KB smem tiles within the 48 KB limit; Br=Bc=64 at d=64, 32/32 at d=128); MIT; 4 stars, 0 forks, exactly 2 commits both on 2026-07-27 (initial + V2 register-fused DESIGN.md doc); perf on RTX 2070: ~1.4 TFLOPS = ~5% of the 28.5 TFLOPS roofline, 2.4-2.6x over its own scalar baseline, but ~10-13x SLOWER than PyTorch SDPA-efficient in isolation; +27% e2e on Qwen2-0.5B (31-33 -> 40-42 tok/s) purely from O(N) memory (29.5 vs 566.4 MB at 4K = 19.2x traffic reduction); causal pruning removes 40-50% of work; GQA/MQA via K/V head expansion; head_dim 64/128 only; NO backward, varlen, sliding window, or INT8 KV (FP16 only, decode falls back to SDPA); correctness max err <5e-4 to <2e-3 vs SDPA; a V2 register-fused variant claiming 5.0 TFLOPS (12.7x over this baseline) is referenced as a related repo but is not in this repo [uncertain]. TRANSFER LANES (the unmanaged surface): (a) FlashQLA sm75 prefill adaptation - exists, integrated in the weicj fork for the Qwen3.6 prefill profile, and honestly measured by its own author at +7.17% prefill e2e. (b) TurboQuant/INT8 KV - upstream vLLM lane is OPEN and unmerged: forum thread 2026-03-31 (discuss.vllm.ai/t/2503) states mainline has no TurboQuant, it is being built as --kv-cache-dtype (issue #38171 'Add TurboQuant Support for KV Cache Quantization', PR #38280 'Add TurboQuant'), nothing merged as of 2026-09-07; nightly dev builds already reject turboquant_4bit_nc on both TRITON_ATTN and FLASH_ATTN ('kv_cache_dtype not supported', issue #40094, opened 2026-04-17, open, untriaged, L4); community interim: mitkox/vllm-turboquant (RTX A6000/SM86), varjoranta/turboquant-vllm (fused CUDA kernels, 3.8x KV), PyPI turboquant-plus-vllm (4.3x weight / 3.7x KV, zero calibration), Intel Arc Pro B70 via a 3-file patch on top of 'PR-38479' [uncertain: that PR identifier, not named in the forum thread]; the weicj fork carries TurboQuant K8V4 + INT8 KV privately on its FlashInfer path; ik_llama's impl has unvalidated CUDA kernels. (c) MTP routing - upstream vLLM has day-0 Qwen3-Next MTP via --speculative-config {method: mtp} (blog 2025-09-11); the current Qwen3.8-Flash-Next official recipe (requires vLLM 0.29.0+ dedicated image vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next) validates MTP3 only on GB300 TP4/TEP4 and WARNS MTP HURT on 4x H100 (8-36% lower throughput, 32-173% higher per-token latency, ~36% acceptance); open upstream MTP issues: #31186 (illegal memory access, B200, FLASH_ATTN), #35387 (76% latency regression; max_num_scheduled_tokens capped 2048 by spec-decode), #37435 (MTP draft config drops target --hf-overrides, breaking long-context speculation), #40756 (crash at num_spec_tokens=5 on long requests), llm-compressor #1843 (FP8 MTP draft produces no accepted tokens); weicj contributes the task-sensitivity data (house-landed, ~1.4x at K=3 acceptance band); ik_llama contributes per-accepted-token budget charging and NextN MTP for qwen4exp. (d) NVFP4-on-Marlin - the sm75 base is upstream (PRs #29901/#31000, shipped v0.14.0 2026-01-20), but the fp16 path was broken on Turing: issue #33461 (opened 2026-01-31, 2x RTX 2080 Ti, NVFP4 via VLLM_NVFP4_GEMM_BACKEND=marlin outputs garbage, closed not-planned/stale) and #33560 (lm-eval accuracy differences Turing vs Ampere on Qwen3-8B-NVFP4); canonical fix PR #33972 (ir1ka, opened 2026-02-06, MERGED 2026-03-27, commit 148a5c1): apply global_scale in FP32 BEFORE the FP16 cast (overflow occurred on accum.half()) and disable use_fp16_accum for NVFP4; lm-eval evidence: Qwen3-32B-NVFP4 and Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 fp16 ppl restored from NaN to 3.8613/4.5259 vs bf16 baselines 3.8664/4.5282 (MoE Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 was unaffected - the failure was dense-model-specific); competing PR #37135 (opened 2026-03-16, closed unmerged 2026-03-23) proved the subtle trap: its input_global_scale-forwarding half was WRONG - that scale only applies to W4A4 activation quant, and applying it to Marlin's W4A16 flow produced ppl ~10 billion vs 4.5. The weicj fork already validates Qwen3.8 27B FP8/NVFP4 profiles on v0.2.1-pre3 (2026-08-27).
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing-class hardware from each sibling, as of 2026-09-07: (A) weicj fork - the only sibling running a full vLLM serving stack on sm75: dual RTX 2080 Ti 22GB TP2 (NVLink recommended, PCIe P2P baseline), CUDA-graph non-eager TP=2/PP=1 validated on v0.2.x (upstream 0.27.1 base), MTP3 GPTQ-INT4 at 91 tok/s on dual 22GB (house-verified; the README's own host note: i3-9100T/16GB RAM host ~91 tok/s vs ~56 tok/s on dual Xeon X5675 - host CPU materially moves their numbers, a caveat for any hybrid-CPU technique transfer); INT8-KV and TurboQuant K8V4 routes run on the fork's PRIVATE FlashInfer path (upstream floors FlashInfer at SM80 since v0.24.0 per the house turing-engine-upstream-drift ledger - their 'one FlashInfer floor constant' restores it); MXFP4 not viable on SM75 Marlin; Gemma4 INT8/TurboQuant have CUDA-graph fallback/admission issues. (B) FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 - runs standalone on SM75 and inside the weicj GGUF runtime: the 2.1x is real at kernel scope but the author's own whole-request numbers bound the transfer value at prefill +7.17% / decode +0.61% / wall -3.49%; GDN decode is simply not the bottleneck (the host's plan/0007 record already shows the sm75 GDN prefill surface is FMA-bound FLA-Triton, which is exactly the prefill gap this kernel addresses); upstream TileLang FlashQLA path unusable on sm75 (SM90+). (C) ik_llama.cpp - CUDA 'Turing or newer' is first-class: Q8_0/Q4_0/Hadamard KV quant works (incl. with MLA), MTP works for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp) family as of 2026-09-02, hybrid CPU/GPU offload runs models larger than VRAM; BUT it is a GGUF llama.cpp-family engine - techniques transfer as designs (Hadamard KV, MTP budget charging, SWA compression), not as code onto a vLLM fork. (D) johnscheuer FA1 - runs on SM75 but at ~5% roofline and 10-13x slower than SDPA-efficient in isolation; its only e2e win (+27% on a 0.5B model at 4K ctx) comes from memory savings, which FlashInfer-on-sm75 already provides better once the floor constant is restored; head_dim 64/128 only; superseded for serving - value is the documented WMMA tiling / causal-pruning / register-fusion designs for plan/0002's CUDA ladder. ATTENTION-BACKEND CANDIDATE MATRIX on sm75 (house ledger, gates every adopt lane): FLASH_ATTN no (>= 8.0); FLASHINFER the load-bearing leg - floor (7,5) through v0.23.0, raised to (8,0) in v0.24.0 (restore draft PR #46943; flashinfer fixes #3526 merged 2026-07-22 / #3621 open) - uniquely carries fp8 KV (2x capacity) and is the only leg the weicj TurboQuant/INT8-KV routes ride; TRITON_ATTN the only auto-candidate since v0.24.0 but rejects fp8 KV on cc 7.5 and hits the 64 KB smem ceiling at head_dim>128; FLEX_ATTENTION inherits Triton codegen risk; XFORMERS defunct; FlashMLA sm90+ (TRITON_MLA is the only DeepSeek-class option, 'Any' capability); a separate flashinfer issue (#3540) reports NVFP4 code in prefill.cuh breaking sm75 compatibility [uncertain: status]. TRITON CODEGEN PATH (gates the FLA/GDN and Triton fallbacks): pre-Ampere tl.dot lowers to mma.m16n8k8 with FMA fallback; the Triton 3.3.x window crashed f16 ops on cc<8.0 (fixed by #7585, carried >= 3.4), so community practice pins <= 3.2 or verified >= 3.4 - the FMA-bound FLA GDN prefill is precisely why a CUDA-native GDN prefill (adopt from weicj, or rebuild on the kernel ladder) is the only escape. NVFP4-on-Marlin on sm75: viable post-#33972 with dtype float16 (FP32-scale-before-cast epilogue; use_fp16_accum disabled for 4-bit) - W4A16 emulation needs no native FP4/FP8 tensor cores, and per plan/0005 stage 9 the E2M1+E4M3 dequant reference is exact, so oracle-attestation is available on this host.

effort_value.effort_estimate: Split verdict per lane, sized against the house plans. ADOPT (small, 1-2 sessions each): (1) NVFP4-on-Marlin fp16 semantics - verify the fork's pinned Marlin carries the two #33972 behaviors (apply global_scale in FP32 before the FP16 cast; disable use_fp16_accum for NVFP4 / group_size==-1 && num_bits==4), cherry-pick if the pin predates 2026-03-27, plus a registry row and an lm-eval-style regression check; adapter + registry-row size, no new kernel. (2) MTP-on-engine guard rails - assert the three known upstream MTP failure modes are not silently hit on this host's config (#35387's max_num_scheduled_tokens 2048 cap, #37435's draft dropping --hf-overrides, #40756's long-request crash) and record per-task acceptance per the weicj task-sensitivity template; a test row, not code. (3) A standing crosspoll audit row - a dated ledger entry per quarter (or per weicj release, they ship weekly) over the four repos recording technique deltas, upstream-base moves, and maintenance-health changes; half a session each. REBUILD (campaign-sized, already owned elsewhere - do NOT adopt): (4) GDN sm75 chunked-prefill CUDA kernel - the weicj legacy extension is forward-only, lazy-built, no auto-dispatch, and its own author's e2e bound is +7.17% prefill / +0.61% decode; building it on the plan/0002 kernel ladder under plan/0003 oracle discipline fits the house's execution-layer identity and the operator's internal-advancement goal; the adopt version's measured ceiling is the falsifier for scope. (5) TurboQuant KV - defer/rebuild-later: upstream unmerged and backend-gated (needs the FlashInfer leg), ik_llama's CUDA kernels unvalidated, and the maintainer's own Hadamard-q4_0 counter-evidence is unresolved; the cheaper sm75 KV levers (fp8-KV-on-FlashInfer = one constant revert; INT8 KV) come first per the house KV-capacity item. WATCH ONLY: johnscheuer FA1 (read the WMMA/register-fusion designs; not competitive), ik_llama hybrid CPU/GPU (owned by the ktransformers item).
effort_value.unlocks: Lane-by-lane against the operator's Qwen3.8 + Qwen3.8-Next focus: NVFP4 fix semantics unlock the 4-bit dense route for Qwen3.8 27B-class checkpoints on TU102 (W4A16 at half the fp16 weight bytes = direct decode-bandwidth win on the measured 535 GB/s floor, and the E4M3/E2M1 dequant reference is oracle-exact per plan/0005 stage 9 - the one quant format where attestation is cheapest); MTP guard rails protect the ratified MTP3-first decode lever (~1.4x at K=3 acceptance band floor-anchored in MEMORY 2026-09-07) from the upstream regression set that has bitten others; the crosspoll audit row unlocks drift intelligence on the parity yardstick itself - weicj rebased 0.21.0 -> 0.27.1 within a month, so their floor-constant/TurboQuant/FlashQLA patches move continuously and an unwatched yardstick silently invalidates plan/0005 stage-13 parity comparisons; the GDN prefill rebuild unlocks the FMA-bound prefill escape for Qwen3.8-Next-class GDN layers (the plan/0007-recorded gap) on the house's own terms; deferring TurboQuant keeps the 22K+ context envelope achievable via fp8/INT8 KV without importing an unmerged randomized-rotation dependency.
effort_value.dependency_order: First: the engine row (FlashInfer floor revert + pinned sm75-capable FlashInfer) - it gates the weicj-comparable KV routes (TurboQuant/INT8 KV ride FlashInfer) and is owned by the turing-engine-upstream-drift item; nothing on the KV lane should start before it. NVFP4 semantics ride the plan/0002 Marlin campaign at its serving-integration step (kernel already exists upstream; only the pin check + registry row are new). MTP guard rails ride the already-scheduled MTP3-first spec-decode work (MEMORY 2026-09-07: the MTP lever rides this fork's vLLM engine path) - parallel-safe with the NVFP4 row. GDN prefill rebuild depends on the plan/0003 harness (float64 oracle) and the plan/0007 d256-bridge records, and is independent of the engine row (kernel-scope work). TurboQuant is last: needs attention-backend KV plumbing on the FlashInfer leg AND an upstream merge or a fork-carried kernel decision. Fully parallel-safe anytime: the crosspoll audit ledger, the ik_llama technique watch (Hadamard KV design, -md standalone MTP, per-accepted-token budget), and the johnscheuer design reading.
effort_value.risk_notes: Correctness/numerics: (1) NVFP4-on-Marlin - the failure class is QUIET, not crashing: #33560 was an lm-eval accuracy delta and the MoE model passed while dense models NaN'd, i.e. model-class-dependent silent corruption - exactly what float64-oracle gates catch and spot perplexity checks can miss; and the fix direction is genuinely subtle (the wrong half of #37135 - applying input_global_scale to W4A16 - produced ppl ~10 billion), so the adopt must be the #33972 semantics specifically, verified by test not by trust. (2) TurboQuant - randomized orthogonal rotation is a run-to-run nondeterminism source unless the rotation seed is pinned; Lloyd-Max codebook error is statistical; and the strongest available counter-evidence (ikawrakow: Hadamard q4_0 beats TQ at equal footprint) is unpublished-measurement grade - quality claims must be re-verified here, never imported. (3) MTP - the official Qwen3.8-Flash-Next recipe itself documents MTP3 HURTING on 4x H100 (8-36% throughput loss at ~36% acceptance): acceptance is task/model/regime-sensitive, so per-task acceptance recording (weicj task-sensitivity discipline) is a correctness-of-claims requirement, not a nicety; the upstream bug set (#35387/#37435/#40756) is live on current vLLM. (4) FlashQLA adopt-would-be - a lazy-built extension with no auto-dispatch, SM70 compile-only, and an e2e ceiling its own author measured at +0.61% decode. Upstream-drift exposure: weicj's fork is a fast-moving rebase rider (0.21.0 -> 0.27.1 in one month) whose sm75 viability hangs on a private one-constant FlashInfer patch - any technique adopted from them inherits that hidden gate and their release cadence; ik_llama techniques are design-transfer only (GGUF engine, CPU-first); johnscheuer is a two-commit snapshot whose V2 claim is unverifiable in-repo. Peer-number hygiene: all weicj numbers are best-case single-user profiles and enter house records only under the median-of-five cross-restart normalization (MEMORY 2026-09-07).
effort_value.determinism_class: Statistical, not bitwise, across the whole surface - but with three distinct variance mechanisms the gate discipline must separate. (1) NVFP4-on-Marlin: kernel accumulation order is fixed per config (deterministic run-to-run), but use_fp16_accum on sm75 (pre-#33972) vs disabled (post-fix) is a numerics-CLASS change - same inputs, different results - so the pinned-kernel identity belongs in every transcript; the dequant reference (E2M1 LUT, E4M3 scales, FP32 global scale) is exactly representable, giving the float64-oracle an exact ground truth - the strongest attestation available on this surface. (2) TurboQuant: the random orthogonal rotation makes outputs seed-dependent (run-to-run and restart-to-restart variant unless the seed is pinned and persisted); the Hadamard alternative is deterministic-orthogonal; gate discipline: pin rotation seeds, oracle per seed, median-of-N across restarts. (3) MTP: draft-verify rejection sampling is distribution-preserving in exact arithmetic, but accepted-length variance drives e2e token-count/tok-s-run variance - median-of-five decode plus recorded per-task acceptance rates; restart-to-restart adds scheduler batching differences. Cross-cutting: the FlashInfer leg carries autotune plan-selection nondeterminism across warmups/restarts (house record; the official Flash-Next recipe itself passes --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune, adopt that practice); backend swaps (FlashInfer -> TRITON_ATTN fallback) change accumulation/split-K order at fp16-visible scale - statistical-band comparison only; the GDN chunked-solve kernels have fixed per-config accumulation order and the forward-only inference variants are restart-stable.

decision.priority_signal: FOR doing the manage-and-adopt part next: two of the operator's four live surfaces map one-to-one onto cheap, upstream-evidenced adopt lanes (NVFP4 fp16 fix semantics -> Qwen3.8 dense 4-bit route; MTP guard rails -> the ratified MTP3-first decode lever); the parity yardstick (weicj) is itself the richest technique source and ships weekly, so an unmanaged surface means silent yardstick drift exactly when plan/0005 stage 13 depends on it; ik_llama.cpp proves daily on Turing-class CUDA that MTP + GDN + KV-quant designs work; and the audit row is nearly free. AGAINST / scope-limiting: the one big rebuild (GDN sm75 prefill) is bounded by the author's own +7.17% prefill e2e - modest, and only worth it as a kernel-ladder exercise under the house's execution-layer identity, not as a perf emergency; TurboQuant adoption now would import an unmerged, seed-nondeterministic, contested-quality dependency while two cheaper KV levers (fp8 KV, INT8 KV) remain unexhausted; the NVFP4 route competes with the house GPTQ-INT4/W4A16 lane that already ties the DRAM floor; and window-closing risk is LOW for the adopt items (upstream fixes already merged) - this is not a race. Net: land the two adopts + audit row now; keep GDN prefill and TurboQuant gated behind the engine row and the KV-capacity item respectively; treat ik_llama as a technique emitter and johnscheuer as a design reference, nothing more.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 NVFP4 probe, oracle-first, no timing until numerics are proven, under a day on the existing TU102 host: (1) load a dense NVFP4 checkpoint of Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 class (matching the #33972 upstream evidence) through the fork's NVFP4 adapter onto the pinned upstream Marlin kernel with dtype float16; first statically verify the two #33972 semantics are present in the pinned kernel source (global_scale applied in FP32 before the FP16 cast; use_fp16_accum disabled for NVFP4 / group_size==-1 && num_bits==4) - if the pin predates 2026-03-27, cherry-pick and re-verify. (2) Oracle-check one decoder layer's GEMM outputs against the float64 dequant reference of the stored values (E2M1 LUT + E4M3 block scales + FP32 global scale are exactly representable - the reference is exact); assert zero nan/inf. (3) Run the lm-eval lambada_openai equivalent vs a bf16/fp32-recast baseline and require ppl within the statistical band (upstream's own post-fix delta was 4.5259 vs 4.5282 - a tight, falsifiable target; any drift beyond it means a residual sm75 epilogue issue). (4) Only then, median-of-five decode across restarts for throughput, recorded per the house discipline. Falsifier: nan/inf or out-of-band ppl settles adopt-vs-defer for the 4-bit dense route in one day with no new kernel work. Optional companion probe if the GDN prefill rebuild is next in line: time one Qwen3.8-Next-class GDN layer's FLA Triton chunked prefill on this host vs the 535 GB/s DRAM floor to bound the FMA tax, and compare the implied headroom against weicj's +7.17% prefill ceiling before committing campaign effort.
